evidence: src/sqllens/_atomic.py:38-49: mkstemp creates the file (stdlib documents mode 0600, O_EXCL, created before any write) in path.parent. Content is written to that fd, then os.replace renames the tempfile over the destination. A rename keeps the tempfile's inode and mode, so the destination ends up 0600 on POSIX. Windows is explicitly out of scope per the module docstring.

src/sqllens/_atomic.py:38-42 creates the tempfile with tempfile.mkstemp, which opens with O_EXCL and mode 0o600 on POSIX. The fd is created before any content is written (line 45-46). A umask can only remove bits, so the mode is never wider than owner-only. The code sets no mode for Windows, so access follows the directory ACL, which matches the docstring. Hostile input considered: a restrictive umask (0777) gives a mode narrower than 0600, still owner-only or tighter. A FAT-style mount that ignores modes is a filesystem limit, not a case where the tempfile is created with a non-owner-only mode. The claim concerns tempfiles created in this helper, so callers that bypass it are outside the docstring's scope.

config.py:602 sources are [init_settings, env_settings, TomlConfigSettingsSource, ...] with init first. LLMConfig (config.py:94) is a plain BaseModel, not BaseSettings, so a partial dict does not trigger its own source resolution. pydantic-settings combines source outputs with deep_update (nested dicts merged per key, higher-priority source wins), so init llm={'api_key':..} overrides only api_key while model/max_tokens/base_url come from env/TOML, then defaults. This is from my knowledge of pydantic-settings internals; I did not run it. Config.load at config.py:642 uses this, and its docstring (617-618) says other values keep usual precedence. tests/unit/test_local_config_security.py:136 exercises it.

config.py:642 passes llm_api_key via cls(llm={'api_key':...}) (init kwargs) without touching os.environ (only SQLLENS_CONFIG is touched, and restored). settings_customise_sources (602-608) puts init_settings first, then env, then TOML; pydantic-settings deep-merges source dicts, so sibling llm.* fields from env/TOML are kept, and only api_key is overridden, beating SQLLENS_LLM__API_KEY. Other values keep env > toml > default precedence. Deep-merge is library behavior, not re-run here.

cli.py:167-173 wraps the symlink check (raises OSError explicitly) and atomic_write_text in `except OSError` that prints a 'Could not write config' error and raises typer.Exit(code=1). _atomic.py:38-55: mkstemp with a missing/unwritable dir raises FileNotFoundError/PermissionError (OSError subclasses), not ValueError; write/fsync/os.replace failures are OSError (e.g. IsADirectoryError for a directory target). cli.py:170 init uses atomic_write_text. _atomic.py:38-49 uses tempfile.mkstemp (0600), fsync, os.replace, so --force replacement is atomic at 0600 on POSIX. claude_desktop.py: TOML (536-537), cmd (561-562), backup (609,613), JSON (619-620), and reverts (717-738) all call _reject_symlink then an atomic write. Doc text is at docs/internal/installation/claude-desktop-installer.md:139-147. validate_toml (claude_desktop.py:348-352) calls Config.load(toml_path, llm_api_key=api_key); no 'environ' appears anywhere in the file. Config.load (config.py:611) accepts llm_api_key keyword.

run_install writes toml via _atomic_write_text (claude_desktop.py:33 import of sqllens._atomic.atomic_write_text; call at :537). atomic_write_text (_atomic.py:25-27) does content.encode('utf-8') then writes raw bytes in 'wb' mode (:45-47); utf-8 codec adds no BOM. Falsifier: content beginning with U+FEFF would encode to a BOM, but generate_toml (claude_desktop.py:210-211) always starts with the literal '# SQL Lens configuration...' header, with user values only in later quoted fields, so the TOML never begins with U+FEFF.

In run_install (src/sqllens/installers/claude_desktop.py), every generated file goes through sqllens._atomic: TOML via _atomic_write_text (l.537), .cmd via _atomic_write_bytes of cmd_content.encode('utf-8') (l.552,562), merged JSON via _atomic_write_text (l.620). _atomic.py:25-27 encodes with plain 'utf-8' (no BOM) and writes bytes (l.30-48). Adversarial input: a user's pre-existing BOM'd JSON; the backup (l.613) and reverts copy original bytes verbatim, but those are preservation of user data, not installer-generated files, which matches the claim's scope ('users who let the installer generate the file'). Rewritten config JSON is serialized fresh, hence BOM-free.

Head claude_desktop.py:355-357 _reject_symlink raises InstallError for any symlink; it is called at 662 (_read_existing_config), 686 (_read_text_or_none), 696 (_read_bytes_or_none). Base view has no 'symlink' handling in the installer, so symlinked configs/launchers (e.g. dotfile-managed claude_desktop_config.json) were previously read and worked, and now fail. The change is deliberate and documented (docs/internal/installation/claude-desktop-installer.md:145, docs/external/configuration.md:267; test tests/unit/test_local_config_security.py:80-101 expects rejection), but the claim that legitimately symlinked callers are not broken is false.

src/sqllens/config.py only mutates env via os.environ["SQLLENS_CONFIG"] = ... (lines 632, 659) and os.environ.pop (657); no putenv/update/setdefault. Item assignment goes through os._Environ.__setitem__, which the test patches (tests/unit/test_local_config_security.py:113-125). MutableMapping.update/setdefault in CPython call self[key]=value, so they also route through __setitem__. Caveat: os.putenv does NOT route through __setitem__ (the reverse is true), so that parenthetical is inaccurate, but the code never calls putenv, so the assertion is meaningful for what Config.load can do. I did not read installer.validate_toml.
